newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB - Ukrainian livestock sector in decline.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Ukrainian livestock sector in decline.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
KIEV, June 25 - The Ukrainian livestock sector continues to contract, with public sector farms affected the most.
As of June 1, 1997, meat and milk production on public farms had dropped 12 percent and 36 percent respectively compared to 1996 levels.
The situation in the private sector is less dire, with some growth in meat output and only a slight drop in the milk sector.

But cattle and pig inventories are decreasing in both sectors. The year-on-year decline on state farms as of June 1 was very considerable and had reached 20 percent for cattle, 15 percent for cows and 35 percent for pigs.
The feed supply situation is also worse.

As of June 1, the availability of feedstuffs was estimated at 983,000 tonnes, including 235,000 tonnes of compound feeds. This makes about 0.09 tonnes per head (compared to 0.21 tonnes in 1996), including 0.02 tonnes of compound feeds (compared to 0.05 tonnes in 1996).
